title: First Missing Positive
description:
Given an unsorted integer array `nums`, return the smallest positive integer (`>= 1`) that is not present in `nums`.

You must implement an algorithm that runs in `O(n)` time and uses `O(1)` auxiliary space. The array may contain zero, negative numbers, duplicates, and values larger than `nums.length`.
hints: For an array of length n, the smallest missing positive integer must lie in the range [1, n + 1]. Any value <= 0 or > n cannot be the answer.
Use the input array itself as a hash table: place every in-range value v (1 <= v <= n) at index v - 1 by swapping it into position.
Guard against duplicates by only swapping when nums[v - 1] != v. Afterwards, the first index i with nums[i] != i + 1 gives the answer i + 1 (or n + 1 if all match).

examples.explanation: 1 and 2 are present in the array, so the smallest missing positive is 3.
1 is present, while 2 is missing, so return 2.
The smallest positive integer 1 is not in the array.
